title: Finished Pieces Can Be Ticked Off
eyebrow: A finished job is stuck being marked unfinished; you approved the fix and it is being built

actions.fyi: You said let the stage's change count, so it is being built. Nothing on this page is waiting on you.

content.label: What is wrong
content.lead: A job's pieces are refused their tick even after the change is live on your board.

items: A piece of work is ticked off only once a merged change carries that piece's name.
The pieces of one stage are merged together, under the name of the stage.
So a piece never sees its own name, and its tick is refused for good.
The name cannot be added afterwards: the merged change is already shared.

rows: Its three pieces on the work list

content.label: Watched happening, before anything was changed
content.lead: The rule was asked, card by card, which merged change it would accept.

blocks.text: Put the old rule back and two of the three cases go red, while the untouched one stays green. The check now breaks itself on purpose every run, so a case that has quietly stopped watching goes red instead of staying green.

content.label: Why it matters beyond one job
content.lead: Every job that splits into pieces hits this, so the work list drifts away from the truth.

blocks.text: The board is the only place work state lives. A rule that marks finished work unfinished makes it lie, and every job with more than one piece in a stage runs into it.

decisions.title: A piece may be ticked off by the change that carries its stage, and only its stage
decisions.why: The pieces of one stage are pieces of one change, so the change that lands the stage lands all of them. Letting the whole job's name count instead would go back to one change ticking off every stage, which was removed on purpose. Written as one sentence covering both shapes of job, so the strictness of today's shape falls out of the rule rather than being a special case.

decisions.title: The rule gets a case that goes red when it is taken out
decisions.why: A guard that only ever passes is not a guard. One case proves a stage's change ticks its pieces off, a second proves the whole job's name still does not.

decisions.title: Only jobs of the older shape change; today's jobs stay as strict as they are
decisions.why: A job written today hangs its pieces straight off the job itself, so there is no stage above them and nothing widens. Only the older shape, where the pieces sit under the stage, is unstuck — which is exactly the shape that is stuck.

decisions.title: One hole is accepted and written down rather than closed
decisions.why: A change carrying a stage makes every piece of that stage tickable at once, so it cannot tell apart a piece that was genuinely left unfinished. The stage still cannot finish until each piece is ticked with its own written reason, so the gap is a reason nobody wrote honestly, not a silent tick.

next.if_nothing: The fix lands and the tags work finishes ticking itself off. Nothing here is waiting on you.
